newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Overheated Russian shares dip, correction seen.
newsitem.headline: Overheated Russian shares dip, correction seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Tuesday after strong gains in recent weeks, and traders said the correction would continue for several more days until prices fell low enough to attract investors.
But second-tier shares, which lagged behind leading shares in the price rise, edged up.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares fell 1.23 percent to 469.70 on $55.44 million in total market volume.
"There are no buyers in the leading shares -- they are still too expensive," said Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin. "The money is in the second-tier shares."
He said second-tiers rose by about one to two percent.
Elektrosvyaz telecoms company rose to $10.90 from $9.20 on Monday's close, Murmanskelektro telecoms was $3.00 after $2.75 and Yuganskneftegaz oil company rose to $23.30 from $22.70.

"A smooth cooling down, a smooth correction going on," said IK Prospekt corporate securities director Andrei Ippolitov. "Some people are keeping their money to buy if prices fall. Such a situation will continue for about a month."
Traders said leading shares would not fall sharply as there was still enough money on the market and buying would start as soon as prices were cheap enough.

"Blue chips will not fall deeply, maybe about five percent," Galperin said. "There is a lot of money on the market and as soon as prices are down, buyers will immediately appear. But I am not waiting for a sharp rise, especially in blue chips."
UES power utility was $0.4100 after $0.4245 at Monday's close, Mosenergo power utility fell to $1.450 from $1.517 and Rostelekom telecoms company fell to $4.18 from $4.43.
